headline: Serbia Elects a Parliament of Scholars
lede: A student-led opposition movement has won 141 of Serbia’s 250 parliamentary seats, bringing dozens of academics and physicians into government. The experiment now moves from exceptional credentials to the harder work of reforming institutions, funding research, and reversing a long brain drain.

headline: How GCC Chooses a Switch Strategy
lede: A C or C++ switch statement can become a jump table, a bitset, or a branching comparison tree. GCC weighs density, code size, architecture, and probability—then uses dynamic programming to assemble the profitable pieces.

headline: Technology Works Better When It Waits
lede: Digital minimalism is less about rejecting devices than reclaiming the terms of their use. Offline tools, local software, and deliberate limits offer a quieter alternative to feeds designed to capture attention and data.
pullquote: The best digital tools return control to the person using them.

headline: This Story Box Puts Families in Control
lede: Marelleo turns an ESP32, NFC tags, an SD card, and a small speaker into an open audio player for children. Its journey from breadboard to custom PCB records the practical lessons—battery safety, enclosure design, and rollback-ready updates—that make a hobby build dependable.

headline: A Nintendo Wii Boots Classic Mac OS
lede: The GameCube and Wii were never Apple machines, but their PowerPC hardware provides an unexpected home for Mac OS 7.6. Reverse-engineered firmware, memory maps, interrupts, and drivers turn a familiar console into a working window onto computing history.

headline: A Rust Tool Challenges Cloudflare’s Gate
lede: `cfsolve` obtains Turnstile tokens and clearance cookies without launching a headless browser. It emulates supported browser profiles from the command line or embedded Rust, but its fingerprints—and its usefulness—remain vulnerable to the next change in the challenge system.

headline: Binance Loses Billions in Twenty Minutes
lede: Attackers drained roughly $6.3 billion from Binance-controlled hot wallets across at least 10 blockchains after at least 36 hours of preparation. The speed of the theft exposed the difficult boundary between centralized custody, rapid laundering, and the promise of crypto irreversibility.

headline: Northflank Tells Customers to Rotate Everything
lede: A breach may have exposed decrypted environment variables and stored secrets across customer systems. Revoke and rotate credentials, inspect billing and usage logs, and treat every affected key as compromised until the investigation is complete.

headline: Scribd Reports Exposure Across Four Services
lede: Scribd says an unauthorized party may have accessed email addresses, payment history, and partial card details across Scribd, SlideShare, Everand, and Fable. Full card numbers and passwords were reportedly spared; the remaining data is still useful fuel for targeted phishing.

headline: Lean Gives AI Code a Proof Obligation
lede: Formal verification can check whether software satisfies its stated properties across every permitted input, rather than only the cases testing happens to cover. Lean and related tools may help AI-generated systems become more trustworthy—but only when humans specify the right behavior and maintain the proof.
